purpose: Cache prepared native spacing expressions; both builds implement percentage spacing and apply the same declarations.

method.frequency_control: Uncontrolled boost/governor; shared machine. Paired sampling reduces drift, but intervals do not model systematic host interference.
method.compiler: rustc opt-level=2 debuginfo=0, identical frozen native dependencies and support crates on both sides
method.ci_method: 5000 bootstrap resamples of paired percentage changes; deterministic seed 173, median, 2.5/97.5 percentiles; no multiple-comparison adjustment. Diagnostic evidence, not a universal performance claim.
method.combined_metric: all_samples sums the five sample medians per invocation; it is cumulative sample time, not a simultaneous page or peak.
method.spacing_workloads: Existing EPUB benchmark source unchanged. Both use 64 classes at font-size:16px with prior length fallbacks. The output-equivalent workload uses letter-spacing:0% and word-spacing:calc(2px - 6.25%); the added-feature workload uses 2% and calc(2px + 5%). Both builds support all declarations and compute the same values as each other. Both workloads measure the same feature work before and after expression caching. The feature workload intentionally differs from the equivalent workload, but is identical between builds.

interpretation: Positive timing percentages mean slower; intervals containing zero are inconclusive, not equivalence.
Mixed stylesheet expressions reuse an immutable native AST. Font-dependent values resolve per element. Inline and substituted values retain element-local native parsing.

The cache retains native ASTs and map entries. Allocations and peak bytes are recorded even when time improves. Cached-run counters begin after program warmup and exclude cache memory already retained; unchanged cached peak does not mean zero cache memory cost.
Both builds share freshly frozen current support crates, including unrelated font-metric work already in the workspace. Historical pre-spacing binaries are not controlled comparators for this run.
The two CSS fixture families retain historical names. Both before and after builds apply the same percentage declarations in each family. No pixel comparison was run.
Shared host frequency/load and code layout limit generalization. No adjustment for multiple comparisons.

initial_phase.followup: A repeated 1.7-3.4% normalization-retry slowdown and extra preparation work prompted a revision. Cache copying now scans declarations only for fragments with cached expressions; ordinary fragments retain the original range-copy loop. All earlier measurements remain recorded.
